extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: As part of the claim adjudication process, we use Optum's Emergency Department Claim Analyzer

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: (EDC) to evaluate the level of the emergency room visit submitted. The goal of the EDC Analyzer is to

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: determine the appropriate facility level of service for emergency department visits based on a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: consistent, objective, and automated methodology. The EDC Analyzer evaluates claim information to

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: identify the intensity of services provided during the emergency department visit and assigns a facility

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: level accordingly. This evaluation is not a medical necessity determination. Medical record review is not

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: performed and does not affect the outcome.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: For a more in-depth look at the Optum Emergency Department Claim Analyzer, refer to the Optum EDC

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: The EDC Analyzer will adjust the code and reimburse at the calculated visit level. This change will

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: be clearly identified on your remittance advice with two column headings: "Billed Proc" and "Paid

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: For example, if you submit a claim with CPT® 99285 and the relevant claim data only supports

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: paying 99284, your RA will show 99285 in the "billed proc" column and 99284 in the "paid proc"

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Claims are exempt from the EDC Analyzer when any of the following are true:

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● The member is admitted as an inpatient;

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● The member expires in the emergency room (discharge status ʻ20ʼ);

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● The member received Critical Care services;

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● The member is discharged/transferred to another care setting (discharge status 03, 04, 05, 06,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● The claim has certain diagnosis codes that most oen necessitate extended resource usage

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: (e.g., substance abuse, sexual assault, mental heath) when treated in the ED.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: We process claims according to Medicare OPPS payment rules, including the use of Ambulatory

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Payment Classification (APC) groupings, Payment Status Indicators (SI), and the packaging of

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: services. Please refer to your contract for specific details.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: In order to process payment, your claims must be submitted on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or the X12 837I

extracted_content.content: electronic equivalent and include the following data elements:

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: follow our Provider Dispute process outlined in your provider manual.
